Let \(p=101\). We want

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}2^{-\lfloor pk/d\rfloor}.
\]

For a positive integer \(m\), let \(N_m\) be the number of pairs \((d,k)\) with \(1\le d\le p-1,\ k\ge 1\) such that

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{pk}{d}\right\rfloor=m.
\]

Then

\[
S=\sum_{m=1}^{\infty} N_m2^{-m}.
\]

For fixed \(d\), the condition is

\[
m\le \frac{pk}{d}<m+1
\iff
\frac{dm}{p}\le k<\frac{d(m+1)}{p}.
\]

Thus the number of such positive integers \(k\) is

\[
\left\lceil \frac{d(m+1)}{p}\right\rceil-\left\lceil \frac{dm}{p}\right\rceil.
\]

Define

\[
F(t)=\sum_{d=1}^{p-1}\left\lceil \frac{dt}{p}\right\rceil.
\]

Then

\[
N_m=F(m+1)-F(m).
\]

Now write \(t=pr+s\) with \(0\le s\le p-1\). Since \(p=101\) is prime,

\[
F(pr)=\frac{rp(p-1)}2,
\]

and for \(1\le s\le p-1\),

\[
F(pr+s)=\frac{p-1}{2}(pr+s+1).
\]

Therefore, for \(m\ge1\),

\[
N_m=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{p-1}{2}, & m\equiv 1,2,\dots,p-2 \pmod p,\\[6pt]
0, & m\equiv p-1 \pmod p,\\[4pt]
p-1, & m\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\end{cases}
\]

Hence

\[
S=\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}
\left(
\frac{p-1}{2}\sum_{s=1}^{p-2}2^{-(pr+s)}
+(p-1)2^{-p(r+1)}
\right).
\]

Using

\[
\sum_{s=1}^{p-2}2^{-s}=1-2^{-(p-2)},
\qquad
\sum_{r=0}^{\infty}2^{-pr}=\frac1{1-2^{-p}},
\]

we get

\[
S=\frac{\frac{p-1}{2}(1-2^{-(p-2)})+(p-1)2^{-p}}{1-2^{-p}}.
\]

Simplifying,

\[
S=(p-1)\frac{1/2-2^{-p}}{1-2^{-p}}
=(p-1)\frac{2^{p-1}-1}{2^p-1}.
\]

Substituting \(p=101\),

\[
S=100\cdot \frac{2^{100}-1}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
S=50-\frac{50}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
